cuckoobud: A species of Ranunculus (R. bulbosus); -- called also butterflower, buttercup, kingcup, goldcup. Shak.
cursed: Deserving a curse; execrable; hateful; detestable; abominable. Let us fly this cursed place. Milton. This cursed quarrel be no more renewed. Dryden.
curfew: 1. The ringing of an evening bell, originally a signal to the inhabitants to cover fires, extinguish lights, and retire to rest, -- instituted by William the Conqueror; also, the bell itself. He begins at curfew, and walks till the first cock. Shak. The village curfew, as it tolled profound. Campbell. 2. A utensil for covering the fire.
cutlet: A piece of meat, especially of veal or mutton, cut for broiling.
curvilinead: An instrument for drawing curved lines.
cultrivorous: Devouring knives; swallowing, or pretending to swallow, knives; -- applied to persons who have swallowed, or have seemed to swallow, knives with impunity. Dunglison.
cudbear: 1. A powder of a violet red color, difficult to moisten with water, used for making violet or purple dye. It is prepared from certain species of lichen, especially Lecanora tartarea. Ure. 2. (Bot.) A lichen (Lecanora tartarea), from which the powder is obtained.
cuish: Defensive armor for the thighs. [ Written also cuisse, and quish.]
curialism: The wiew or doctrins of the ultramontane party in the Latin Church. Gladstone.
cuscus: A soft grass (Pennisetum typhoideum) found in all tropical regions, used as food for men and cattle in Central Africa.
cubooctahedral: Presenting a combination of a cube and an octahedron.
cubebic: Pertaining to, or derived from, cubebs; as, cubebic acid (a soft olive-green resin extracted from cubebs).
curvature: 1. The act of curving, or the state of being bent or curved; a curving or bending, normal or abnormal, as of a line or surface from a rectilinear direction; a bend; a curve. Cowper. The elegant curvature of their fronds. Darwin. 2.
curship: The state of being a cur; one who is currish. [Jocose] How durst he, I say, oppose thy curship! Hudibras.
curvicaudate: Having a curved or crooked tail.
cutaway: Having a part cut off or away; having the corners rounded or cut away. Cutaway coat, a coat whose skirts are cut away in front so as not to meet at the bottom.
culturemyth: A myth accounting for the discovery of arts and sciences or the advent of a higher civilization, as in the Prometheus myth.
curvilinearity: The state of being curvilinear or of being bounded by curved lines.
cultrated: Sharp-edged and pointed; shaped like a pruning knife, as the beak of certain birds.
cuspidated: Having a sharp end, like the point of a spear; terminating in a hard point; as, a cuspidate leaf.
culmination: 1. The attainment of the highest point of altitude reached by a heavently body; passage across the meridian; transit. 2. Attainment or arrival at the highest pitch of glory, power, etc.
culler: One who piks or chooses; esp., an inspector who select wares suitable for market.
curtsy: Same as Courtesy, an act of respect.
cure: 1. Care, heed, or attention. (old) Of study took he most cure and most heed. Chaucer. Vicarages of greatcure, but small value. Fuller. 2. Spiritual charge; care of soul; | 1. To heal; to restore to health, soundness, or sanity; to make well; -- said of a patient. The child was cured from that very hour. Matt. xvii. 18. 2. To subdue or remove by remedial means;
cumulostratus: A form of cloud. See Cloud.
cuppy: 1. Hollow; cuplike; also, full of cups, or small depressions. 2. Characterized by cup shakes; -- said of timber.
cursores: (a) An order of running birds including the ostrich, emu, and allies; the Ratitaæ. (b) A group of running spiders; the wolf spiders.
cuculoid: Like or belonging to the cuckoos (Cuculidæ).
curve: Bent without angles; crooked; curved; as, a curve line; a curve surface. | 1. A bending without angles; that wcich is bent; a flexure; as, a curve in a railway or canal. 2. (Geom.) A line described according to some low, and having no finite portion of it a straight line.
cursorily: In a running or hasty manner; carelessly.
current: 1. Running or moving rapidly. (old) Like the current fire, that renneth Upon a cord. Gower. To chase a creature that was current then In these wild woods, the hart with golden horns. Tennyson. 2. | 1. A flowing or passing; onward motion. Hence: A body of fluid moving continuously in a certain direction; a stream; esp., the swiftest part of it; as, a current of water or of air;
cutout: (a) (Telegraphy) A species of switch for changing the current from one circuit to another, or for shortening a circuit. (b) (Elec.) A divice for breaking or separating a portion of circuit.
curialist: One who belongs to the ultramontane party in the Latin Church. Shipley.
cudgeler: One who beats with a cudgel. [Written also cudgeller.]
curricle: 1. A small or short course. Upon a curricle in this world depends a long course of the next. Sir T. Browne. 2. A two-wheeled chaise drawn by two horses abreast.
curly: Curling or tending to curl; having curls; full of ripples; crinkled.
cucurbitive: Having the shape of a gourd seed; -- said of certain small worms.
curled: Having curls; curly; sinuous; wavy; as, curled maple (maple having fibers which take a sinnuous course). Curled hair (Com.), the hair of the manes and tails of horses, prepared for upholstery purposes. McElrath.
cumin: A dwarf umbelliferous plant, somewhat resembling fennel (Cuminum Cyminum), cultivated for its seeds, which have a bitterish, warm taste, with an aromatic flavor, and are used like those of anise and caraway. [Written also cummin.] Rank-smelling rue, and cumin good for eyes. Spenser. Black cumin (Bot.), a plant (Nigella sativa) with pungent seeds, used by the Afghans, etc.
cuddle: To She cuddles low beneath the brake; Nor would she stay, nor dares she fly. Prior. | To embrace closely; to foundle. Forby.
cutwal: The chief police officer of a large city. [East Indies]
cutlery: 1. The business of a cutler. 2. Edged or cutting instruments, collectively.
curtana: The pointless sword carried before English monarchs at their coronation, and emblematically considered as the sword of mercy; -- also called the sword of Edward the Confessor.
cumulus: One of the four principal forms of clouds. SeeCloud.
culinarily: In the manner of a kitchen; in connection with a kitchen or cooking.
cuesta: A sloping plain, esp. one with the upper end at the crest of a cliff; a hill or ridge with one face steep and the opposite face gently sloping. [Southwestern U. S.]
curbstone: A stone Curbstone broker.See under Broker.
cuckoldry: The state of being a cuckold; the practice of making cuckolds. CUCKOLD'S KNOT Cuck"old's knot` (kk"ldz nt`). (Naut.) A hitch or knot, by which a rope is secured to a spar, the two parts of the rope being crossed and seized together; -- called also cuckold's neck. Ham. Nav. Encyc.
cumshaw: A present or bonus; -- originally applied to that paid on ships which entered the port of Canton. S. Wells Williams.
curability: The state of being curable; curableness.
cushat: The ringdove or wood pigeon. Scarce with cushat's homely song can vie. Sir W. Scott.
cuvette: 1. A pot, bucket, or basin, in which molten plate glass is carried from the melting pot to the casting table. 2. (Fort.) A cunette. 3. (Spectrometry) (Analytical chemistry) A small vessel with at least two flat and transparent sides, used to hold a liquid sample to be analysed in the light path of a spectrometer. Note: The shape and materials vary;
cursedness: 1. The state of being under a curse or of being doomed to execration or to evil. 2. Wickedness; sin; cursing. Chaucer. 3. Shrewishness. "My wife's cursedness." Chaucer.
culturefeatures: The artificial features of a district as distinguished from the natural.
curcumin: The coloring principle of turmeric, or curcuma root, extracted as an orange yellow crystalline substance, C14H14O4, with a green fluorescence. Note: It possesses acid properties and with alkalies forms brownish salts. This change in color from yellow to brown is the characteristic reaction of tumeric paper. See Turmeric paper, under Turmeric.
cudden: 1. A clown; a low rustic; a dolt. (old) The slavering cudden, propped upon his staff. Dryden. 2. (Zoöl.) The coalfish. See 3d Cuddy.
culvert: A transverse drain or waterway of masonry under a road, railroad, canal, etc.; a small bridge.
cureall: A remedy for all diseases, o
cucullate: 1. Hooded; cowled; covered, as with a hood. Sir T. Browne. 2. (Bot.) Having the edges toward the base rolled inward, as the leaf of the commonest American blue violet. 3. (Zoöl.) (a) Having the prothorax elevated so as to form a sort of hood, receiving the head, as in certain insects. (b) Having a hoodlike crest on the head, as certain birds, mammals, and reptiles.
curing: p. a. & vb. n. of Cure. Curing house, a building in which anything is cured; especially, in the West Indies, a building in which sugar is drained and dried.
cultivate: 1. To bestow attention, care, and labor upon, with a view to valuable returns; to till; to fertilize; as, to cultivate soil. 2. To direct special attention to; to devote time and thought to; to foster; to cherish. Leisure . . . to cultivate general literature. Wordsworth. 3. To seek the society of; to court intimacy with.
cubature: The process of determining the solid or cubic contents of a body.
cushiony: Like a cushion; soft; pliable. A flat and cushiony noce. Dickens.
cultivable: Capable of being cultivated or tilled. Todd.
cultivation: 1. The art or act of cultivating; improvement for agricultural purposes or by agricultural processes; tillage; production by tillage. 2. Bestowal of time or attention for self-improvement or for the benefit of others; fostering care. 3. The state of being cultivated; advancement in physical, intellectual, or moral condition; refinement; culture. Italy . . .
cultch: Empty oyster shells and other substances laid down on oyster grounds to furnish points for the attachment of the spawn of the oyster. [Also written cutch.]
cultured: 1. Under culture; cultivated. "Cultured vales." Shenstone. 2. Characterized by mental and moral training; disciplined; refined; well-educated. The sense of beauty in nature, even among cultured people, is less often met with than other mental endowments. I. Taylor. The cunning hand and cultured brain. Whittier.
culdesac: 1. A passage with only one outlet, as a street closed at one end; a blind alley; hence, a trap. 2. (Mil.) a position in which an army finds itself with no way of exit but to the front. 3. (Anat.) Any bag-shaped or tubular cavity, vessel, or organ, open only at one end.
cupping: The operation of drawing blood to or from the surface of the person by forming a partial vacuum over the spot. Also, sometimes, a similar operation for drawing pus from an abscess. Cupping glass, a glass cup in which a partial vacuum is produced by heat, in the process of cupping.
curvet: 1. (Man.) A particular leap of a horse, when he raises both his fore legs at once, equally advanced, and, as his fore legs are falling, raises his hind legs, so that all his legs are in the air at… | 1. To make a curvet; to leap; to bound. 'Oft and high he did curvet." Drayton. 2. To leap and frisk; to frolic. Shak.
curule: 1. Of or pertaining to a charoit. 2. (Rom. Antiq.) Of or pertaining to a kind of chair appropriated to Roman magistrates and dignitaries; pertaining to, having, or conferring, the right to sit in the curule chair; hence, official. Note: The curule chair was usually shaped like a camp stool, and provided with curved legs.
cumacea: An order of marine Crustacea, mostly of small size.
curative: Relating to, or employed in, the cure of diseases; tending to cure. Arbuthnot.
culinary: Relating to the kitchen, or to the art of cookery; used in kitchens; as, a culinary vessel; the culinary art.
cuneated: Wedge-shaped; (Bot.), wedge-shaped, with the point at the base; as, a cuneate leaf.
cursorial: (a) Adapted to running or walking, and not to prehension; as, the limbs of the horse are cursorial. See Illust. of Aves. (b) Of or pertaining to the Cursores.
curiality: The privileges, prerogatives, or retinue of a court. (old) Bacon.
cumidine: A strong, liquid, organic base, C3H7.C6H4.NH2, homologous with aniline.
cumulative: 1. Composed of parts in a heap; forming a mass; agregated. "As for knowledge which man receiveth by teaching, it is cumulative, njt original." Bacon 2. Augmenting, gaining, or giving force, by successive additions; as, a cumulative argument, i. e., one whose force increases as the statement proceeds. The argument . . .
cupellation: The act or process of refining gold or silver, etc., in a cupel. Note: The process consist in exposing the cupel containing the metal to be assayed or refined to a hot blast, by which the lead, copper, tin, etc., are oxidized, dissolved, and carried down into the porous cupel, leaving the unoxidizable precious metal.
cuminic: Pertaining to, or derived from, cumin, or from oil of caraway; as, cuminic acid. Cuminic acid (Chem.), white crystalline substance, C3H7.C6H4.CO2H, obtained from oil of caraway.
currish: Having the qualities, or exhibiting the characteristics, of a cur; snarling; quarrelsome; snappish; churlish; hence, also malicious; malignant; brutal. Thy currish spirit Governed a wolf. Shak. Some currish plot, -- some trick. Lockhart. -- Cur"rish*ly, adv. -- Cur"rish*ness, n.
cucurbite: A vessel of flask for distillation, used with, or forming part of, an alembic; a matrass; -- originally in the shape of a gourd, with a wide mouth. See Alembic.
culmen: 1. Top; summit; acme. R. North. 2. (Zoöl.) The dorsal ridge of a bird's bill.
currycomb: A kind of card or comb having rows of metallic teeth or serrated ridges, used in curryng a horse.
cuirbouilli: In decorative art, boiled leather, fitted by the process to receive impressed patterns, like those produced by chasing metal, and to retain the impression permanently.
cullyism: The state of being a cully. Less frequent instances of eminent cullyism. Spectator.
cuddy: 1. An ass; esp., one driven by a huckster or greengrocer. [Scot.] 2. Hence: A blockhead; a lout. Hood. 3. (Mech.) A lever mounted on a tripod for lifting stones, leveling up railroad ties, etc. | A small cabin: also, the galley or kitchen of a vessel.
curvation: The act of bending or crooking.
cultirostral: Having a bill shaped like the colter of a plow, or like a knife, as the heron, stork, etc.
curdy: Like curd; full of curd; coagulated. "A curdy mass." Arbuthnot.
culverin: A long cannon of the 16th century, usually an 18-pounder with serpent-shaped handles. Trump, and drum, and roaring culverin. Mac
culasse: The lower faceted portion of a brilliant-cut diamond.
cuckoldly: Having the qualities of a cuckold; mean-spirited; sneaking. Shak.
cuminol: A liquid, C3H7.C6H4.CHO, obtained from oil of caraway; -- called also cuminic aldehyde.
cunningman: A fortune teller; one who pretends to reveal mysteries. (old) Hudibras.
curvirostres: A group of passerine birds, including the creepers and nuthatches.
cupuliferous: Of, pertaining to, or resembling, the family of plants ot which the oak and the chestnut are examples, -- trees bearing a smooth, solid nut inclosed in some kind of cup or bur; bearing, or furnished with, a cupule.
curator: 1. One who has the care and superintendence of anything, as of a museum; a custodian; a keeper. 2. One appointed to act as guardian of the estate of a person not legally competent to manage it, or of an absentee; a trustee; a guardian.
cuttle: 1. (Zoöl.) A cephalopod of the genus Sepia, having an internal shell, large eyes, and ten arms furnished with denticulated suckers, by means of which it secures its prey. The name is sometimes applied to dibranchiate cephalopods generally.
cuirassed: 1. Wearing a cuirass. 2. (Zoöl) Having a covering of bony plates, resembling a cuirass;- said of certain fishes.
culver: A dove. "Culver in the falcon's fist." Spenser. | A culverin. Falcon and culver on each tower Stood prompt their deadly hail to shower. Sir W. Scott.
cudweed: A small composite plant with cottony or silky stem and leaves, primarily a species of Gnaphalium, but the name is now given to many plants of different genera, as Filago, Antennaria, etc.; cottonweed.
cucujo: The fire beetle of Mexico and the West Indies.
cursoriness: The quality of being cursory; superficial performance; as, cursoriness of view.
curlew: A wading bird of the genus Numenius, remarkable for its long, slender, curved bill. Note: The common European curlew is N. arquatus. The long-billed (N. longirostris), the Hudsonian (N. Hudsonicus), and the Eskimo curlew (N. borealis, are American species. The name is said to imitate the note of the European species. Curlew Jack (Zoöl.) the whimbrel or lesser curlew.
cumbersome: 1. Burdensome or hindering, as a weight or drag; embarrassing; vexatious; cumbrous. To perform a cumbersome obedience. Sir. P. Sidney. 2. Not easily managed; as, a cumbersome contrivance or machine. He holds them in utter contempt, as lumbering, cumbersome, circuitous. I. Taylor. -- Cum"ber*some*ly, adv. -- Cum"ber*some*ness,n.
curling: 1. The act or state of that which curls; as, the curling of smoke when it rises; the curling of a ringlet; also, the act or process of one who curls something, as hair, or the brim of hats. 2. A scottish game in which heavy weights of stone or iron are propelled by hand over the ice towards a mark. Curling . . .
cutgrass: A grass with leaves having edges furnished with very minute hooked prickles, which form a cutting edge; one or more species of Leersia.
cufic: Of or pertaining to the older characters of the Arabic language. [Written also Kufic.]
cuckingstool: A kind of chair formerly used for punishing scolds, and also dishonest tradesmen, by fastening them in it, usually in front of their doors, to be pelted and hooted at by the mob, but sometimes to be taken to the water and ducked; -- called also a castigatory, a tumbrel, and a trebuchet; and often, but not so correctly, a ducking stool. Sir. W. Scott.
cucumber: A creeping plant, and its fruit, of several species of the genus Cucumis, esp. Cucumis sativus, the unripe fruit of which is eaten either fresh or picked. Also, similar plants or fruits of several other genera. See below. Bitter cucumber (Bot.), the Citrullus or Cucumis Colocynthis. SeeColocynth. -- Cucumber beetle.
culprit: 1. One accused of, or ar An author is in the condition of a culprit; the public are his judges. Prior. 2. One quilty of a fault; a criminal.
cutling: The art of making edged tools or cutlery. (old) Milton.
cubilose: A mucilagenous secretion of certain birds found as the characteristic ingredient of edible bird's-nests.
cursorary: Cursory; hasty. (old) With a cursorary eye o'erglanced the articles. Shak.
culpa: Negligence or fault, as distinguishable from dolus (deceit, fraud), which implies intent, culpa being imputable to defect of intellect, dolus to defect of heart. Wharton.
curiousness: 1. Carefulness; painstaking. (old) My father's care With curiousness and cost did train me up. Massinger. 2. The state of being curious; exactness of workmanship; ingenuity of contrivance. 3. Inquisitiveness; curiosity.
cubhood: The state of being a cub. [Jocose] "From cubhood to old age." W. B. Dawkins.
curvirostral: Having a crooked beak, as the crossbill.
cubicular: Belonging to a chamber or bedroom. (old) Howell.
cucumiform: Having the form of a cucumber; having the form of a cylinder tapered and rounded at the ends, and either straight or curved.
cultriform: Shaped like a pruning knife; cultrate.
culm: The stalk or stem of grain and grasses (including the bamboo), jointed and usually hollow. | (a) Mineral coal that is not bituminous; anthracite, especially when found in small masses. (b) The waste of the Pennsylvania anthracite mines, consisting of fine coal, dust, etc., and used as fuel.
cuttooplate: A hood over the end of a wagon wheel hub to keep dirt away from the axle.
culminant: Being vertical, or at the highest point of altitude; hence, predominant.
cuneiform: 1. Wedge-shaped; as, a cuneiform bone; -- especially applied to the wedge-shaped or arrowheaded characters of ancient Persian and Assyrian inscriptions. See Arrowheaded. 2. | 1. The wedge-shaped characters used in ancient Persian and Assyrian inscriptions. I. Taylor (The Alphabet). 2. (Anat.) (a) One of the three tarsal bones supporting the first, second third…
cushionless: Hot furnished with a cushion. Rows of long, cushionless benches, supplying the place of pews. Hawthorne.
cubical: 1. Having the form or properties of a cube; contained, or capable of being contained, in a cube. 2. (Crystallog.) Isometric or monometric; as, cubic cleavage. See Crystallization. Cubic equation, an equation in which the highest power of the unknown quantity is a cube. -- Cubic foot, a volume equivalent to a cubical solid which measures a foot in each of its dimensions.
cultus: Established or accepted religious rites or usages of worship; state of religious development. Cf.Cult, 2.
cultuscod: See Cod, and Buffalo cod, under Buffalo.
culmiferous: Having jointed stems or culms. | Containing, or abounding in, culm or glance coal.
customhouse: The building where customs and duties are paid, and where vessels are entered or cleared. Customhouse broker, an agent who acts for merchants in the business of entering and clearing goods and vessels.
cuspidor: Any ornamental vessel used as a spittoon; hence, to avoid the common term, a spittoon of any sort.
curbroof: A roof having a double slope, or composed, on each side, of two parts which have unequal inclination; a gambrel roof.
customable: 1. Customary. (old) Sir T. More. 2. Subject to the payment of customs; dutiable.
cuckoopint: A plant of the genus Arum (A. maculatum); the European wake- robin.
currency: 1. A continued or uninterrupted course or flow like that of a sream; as, the currency of time. (old) Ayliffe. 2. The state or quality of being current; general acceptance or reception; a passing from person to person, or from hand to hand; circulation; as, a report has had a long or general currency; the currency of bank notes. 3.
curdle: 1. To change into curd; to coagulate; as, rennet causes milk to curdle. Thomson. 2. To thicken; to congeal. Then Mary could feel her heart's blood curdle cold. Southey. | 1. To change into curd; to cause to coagulate. "To curdle whites of eggs" Boyle. 2. To congeal or thicken. My chill blood is curdled in my veins. Dryden.
cuspidate: Having a sharp end, like the point of a spear; terminating in a hard point; as, a cuspidate leaf.
custody: 1. A keeping or guarding; care, watch, inspection, for keeping, preservation, or security. A fleet of thirty ships for the custody of the narrow seas. Bacon. 2. Judicial or penal safe-keeping. Jailer, take him to thy custody. Shak. 3. State of being guarded and watched to prevent escape; restraint of liberty; confinement; imprisonment.
cupbearer: 1. One whose office it is to fill and hand the cups at an enterainment. 2. (Antiq.) One of the attendants of a prince or noble, permanently charged with the performance of this office for his master. "I was the king's cupbearer." Neh. i. 11.
curtail: To cut off the end or tail, or any part, of; to shorten; to abridge; to diminish; to reduce. I, that am curtailed of this fair proportion. Shak. Our incomes have been curtailed; | The scroll termination of any architectural member, as of a step, etc.
curse: 1. To call upon divine or supernatural power to send injury upon; to imprecate evil upon; to execrate. Thou shalt not . . . curse the ruler of thy people. Ex. xxii. 28. | To utter imprecations or curses; to affirm or deny with imprecations; to swear. Then began he to curse and to swear. Matt. xxi. 74. His spirits hear me, And yet I need must curse. Shak.
curatrix: 1. A woman who cures. 2. A woman who is a guardian or custodian. Burrill.
curvate: Bent in a regular form; curved.
cutchery: A hindoo hall of justice. Malcom.
cubbridgehead: A bulkhead on the forecastle and half deck of a ship.
cutin: The substance which, added to the material of a cell wall, makes it waterproof, as in cork.
cursory: 1. Running about; not stationary. (old) 2. Characterized by haste; hastily or superficially performed; slight; superficial; careless. Events far too important to be treated in a cursory manner. Hallam.
curassow: A large gallinaceous bird of the American genera Crax, Ourax, etc., of the family Cracidæ. Note: The crested curassow (Crax alector) is black, and about the size of a small hen-turkey, with an erectile crest of curled feathers. It ranges from Mexico to Brazil.
cultivator: 1. One who cultivates; as, a cultivator of the soil; a cultivator of literature. Whewell. 2. An agricultural implement used in the tillage of growing crops, to loosen the surface of the earth and kill the weeds; esp., a triangular frame set with small shares, drawn by a horse and by handles.
culpatory: Expressing blame; censuring; reprehensory; inculpating. Adjectives . . . commonly used by Latian authors in a culpatory sense. Walpole.
cursedly: In a cursed manner; miserably; in a manner to be detested; enormously. [Low]
cuibono: Lit., for whose benefit; incorrectly understood, it came to be used in the sense, of what good or use; and hence, (what) purpose; object; specif., the ultimate object of life.
cushion: 1. A case or bag stuffed with some soft and elastic material, and used to sit or recline upon; a soft pillow or pad. Two cushions stuffed with straw, the seat to raise. Dryden. 2. | 1. To seat or place on, or as on a cushion. Many who are cushioned on thrones would have remained in obscurity. Bolingbroke. 2. To furnish with cushions; as, to cushion a chaise. 3.
curry: 1. To dress or prepare for use by a process of scraping, cleansing, beating, smoothing, and coloring; -- said of leather. 2. To dress the hair or coat of (a horse, ox, or the like) with a currycomb… | 1. (Cookery) A kind of sauce much used in India, containing garlic, pepper, ginger, and other strong spices. 2. A stew of fowl, fish, or game, cooked with curry. Curry powder (Cookery), a condiment…
cuproid: (Crystalloq.) A solid related to a tetrahedron, and contained under twelve equal triangles.
cupule: 1. (Bot.) A cuplet or little cup, as the acorn; the husk or bur of the filbert, chestnut, etc. 2. (Zoöl.) A sucker or acetabulum.
cuttystool: 1. A low stool [Scot.] 2. A seat in old Scottish churches, where offenders were made to sit, for public rebuke by the minister.
cuttlefish: 1. (Zoöl.) A cephalopod of the genus Sepia, having an internal shell, large eyes, and ten arms furnished with denticulated suckers, by means of which it secures its prey. The name is sometimes applied to dibranchiate cephalopods generally.
culpable: 1. Deserving censure; worthy of blame; faulty; immoral; criminal. State Trials (1413). If he acts according to the best reason he hath, he is not culpable, though he be mistaken in his measures. Sharp. 2. Guilty; as, clpable of a crime. (old) Spenser. -- Cul"pa*ble*ness, n. -- Cul"pa*bly, adv.
currant: 1. A small kind of seedless raisin, imported from the Levant, chiefly from Zante and Cephalonia; -- used in cookery. 2. The acid fruit or berry of the Ribes rubrum or common red currant, or of its variety, the white currant. 3. (Bot.) A shrub or bush of several species of the genus Ribes (a genus also including the gooseberry); esp., the Ribes rubrum.
curacao: A liqueur, or cordial, flavored with orange peel, cinnamon, and mace; -- first made at the island of Curaçcao.
curtation: The interval by which the curtate distance of a planet is less than the true distance.
curvated: Bent in a regular form; curved.
cub: 1. A young animal, esp. the young of the bear. 2. Jocosely or in contempt, a boy or girl, esp. an awkward, rude, illmannered boy. O, thuo dissembling cub! what wilt thou be When time hath sowed a… | To bring forth; -- said of animals, or in contempt, of persons. "Cubb'd in a cabin." Dryden.
curvinerved: Having the ribs or the veins of the leaves curved; -- called also curvinervate and curve-veined.
cun: To con (a ship). (old) | To know. See Con. (old)
cureless: Incapable of cure; incurable. With patience undergo A cureless ill, since fate will have it so. Dryden.
cushiontire: A thick solid-rubber tire, as for a bicycle, with a hollow groove running lengthwise on the inside.
curculio: One of a large group of beetles (Rhynchophora) of many genera; -- called also weevils, snout beetles, billbeetles, and billbugs. Many of the species are very destructive, as the plum curculio, the corn, grain, and rice weevils, etc.
culturist: 1. A cultivator. 2. One who is an advocate of culture. The culturists, by which term I mean not those who esteem culture (as what intelligent man does notJ. C. Shairp
curiosity: 1. The state or quality or being curious; nicety; accuracy; exactness; elaboration. (old) Bacon. When thou wast in thy gilt and thy perfume, they mocked thee for too much curiosity. Shak. A screen accurately cut in tapiary work . . . with great curiosity. Evelin. 2. Disposition to inquire, investigate, or seek after knowledge;
curari: A black resinoid extract prepared by the South American Indians from the bark of several species of Strychnos (S. toxifera, etc.). It sometimes has little effect when taken internally, but is quickly fatal when introduced into the blood, and used by the Indians as an arrow poison. [Written also urari, woorali, woorari, etc.]
cuisine: 1. The kitchen or cooking department. 2. Manner or style of cooking.
cunning: 1. Knowing; skillfull; dexterous. "A cunning workman." Ex. xxxviii. 23. "Tis beauty truly blent, whose red and white Nature's own sweet and cunning hand laid on. Shak. Esau was a cunning hunter. | 1. Knowledge; art; skill; dexterity. (old) Let my right hand forget her cunning. Ps. cxxxvii. 5. A carpenter's desert Stands more in cunning than in power. Chapman. 2.
cutting: 1. The act or process of making an incision, or of severing, felling, shaping, etc. 2. Something cut, cut off, or cut out, as a twig or | 1. Adapted to cut; as, a cutting tool. 2. Chilling; penetratinn; sharp; as, a cutting wind. 3. Severe; sarcastic; biting; as, a cutting reply.
curst: Froward; malignant; mischievous; malicious; snarling. (old) Though his mind Be ne'er so curst, his tonque is kind. Crashaw.
cutpurse: One who cuts purses for the sake of stealing them or their contents (an act common when men wore purses fastened by a string to their girdles); one who steals from the person; a pickpocket To have an open ear, a quick eye, and a nimble hand, is necessary for a cutpurse. Shak.
curer: 1. One who cures; a healer; a physician. 2. One who prepares beef, fish, etc., for preservation by drying, salting, smoking, etc.
customary: 1. Agreeing with, or established by, custom; established by common usage; conventional; habitual. Even now I met him With customary compliment. Shak. A formal customary attendance upon the offices. | A book containing laws and usages, or customs; as, the Customary of the Normans. Cowell.
culling: 1. The act of one who culls. 2. pl. Anything separated or selected from a mass.
curtailment: The act or result of curtailing or cutting off. Bancroft.
cuprous: Of, pertaining to, or derived from, copper; containing copper; -- said of those compounds of copper in which this element is present in its highest proportion.
cumbrance: Encumbrance. (old) Extol not riches then, the toil of fools, The wise man's cumbrance, if not snare. Milton.
currently: In a current manner; generally; commonly; as, it is currently believed.
cunner: (a) A small edible fish of the Atlantic coast (Ctenolabrus adspersus); -- called also chogset, burgall, blue perch, and bait stealer. [Written also conner.] (b) A small shellfish; the limpet or patella.
curmurring: Murmuring; grumbling; -- sometimes applied to the rumbling produced by a slight attack of the gripes. [Scot.] Burns.
culturable: Capable of, or fit for, being cultivated; capable or becoming cultured. London Spectator.
curtate: Shortened or reduced; -- said of the distance of a planet from the sun or earth, as measured in the plane of the ecliptic, or the distance from the sun or earth to that point where a perpendicular, let fall from the planet upon the plane of the ecliptic, meets the ecliptic. Curtate cycloid. (Math.) See Cycloid.
custos: A keeper; a custodian; a superintendent. (old) Custos rotulorum (r Etym: [LL., keeper of the rolls] (Eng. Law), the principal justice of the peace in a county, who is also keeper of the rolls and records of the sessions of the peace.
curate: One who has the cure souls; originally, any clergyman, but now usually limited to one who assist a rector or vicar Hook. All this the good old man performed alone, He spared no pains, for curate he had none. Dryden.
culverkey: 1. A bunch of the keys or samaras of the ash tree. Wright. 2. An English meadow plant, perhaps the columbine or the bluebell squill (Scilla nutans). (old) A girl cropping culverkeys and cowslips to make garlands. Walton. CULVER'S PHYSIC; CULVER'S ROOT Cul"ver's phys"ic, or Cul"ver's root`. [So called after a Dr.
cumbrous: 1. Rendering action or motion difficult or toilsome; serving to obstruct or hinder; burdensome; clogging. He sunk beneath the cumbrous weight. Swift. That cumbrousand unwieldy style which disfigures English composition so extensively. De Quincey. 2. Giving trouble; vexatious. (old) A clud of cumbrous gnats. Spenser. -- Cum"brous*ly, adv. -- Cum"brous*ness, n.
custom: 1. Frequent repetition of the same act; way of acting common to many; ordinary manner; habitual practice; usage; method of doing or living. And teach customs which are not lawful. Acts xvi. 21. | 1. To make familiar; to accustom. (old) Gray. 2. To supply with customers. (old) Bacon.
cumene: A colorless oily hydrocarbon, C6H5.C3H7, obtained by the distillation of cuminic acid; -- called also cumol.
cuban: Of or pertaining to Cuba or its inhabitants. -- n. A native or an inhabitant of Cuba.
curtilage: A yard, courtyard, or piece of ground, included within the fence surrounding a dwelling house. Burrill.
cupmoss: A kind of lichen, of the genus Cladonia.
currentness: 1. The quality of being current; currency; circulation; general reception. 2. Easiness of pronunciation; fluency. (old) When currentness [combineth] with staidness, how can the language . . . sound other than most full of sweetness Camden.
cutaneous: Of pertaining to the skin; existing on, or affecting, the skin; as, a cutaneous disease; cutaneous absorption; cutaneous respiration.
curler: 1. One who, or that which, curls. 2. A player at the game called curling. Burns.
culvertailed: United or fastened by a dovetailed joint.
curial: Of or pertaining to the papal curia; as, the curial etiquette of the Vatican. -- n. A member of a curia, esp. of that of Rome or the later Italian sovereignties.
culdee: One of a class of anchorites who lived in various parts of Scotland, Ireland, and Wales. The pure Culdees Were Albyn's earliest priests of God. Campbell.
cummerbund: A sash for the waist; a girdle. [India]
cuinage: The stamping of pigs of tin, by the proper officer, with the arms of the duchy of Cornwall.
cubdrawn: Sucked by cubs. This night, wherein the cub-drawn bear would couch. Shak.
curette: A scoop or ring with either a blunt or a cutting edge, for removing substances from the walls of a cavity, as from the eye, ear, or womb.
cuniform: 1. Wedge-shaped; as, a cuneiform bone; -- especially applied to the wedge-shaped or arrowheaded characters of ancient Persian and Assyrian inscriptions. See Arrowheaded. 2. | 1. The wedge-shaped characters used in ancient Persian and Assyrian inscriptions. I. Taylor (The Alphabet). 2. (Anat.) (a) One of the three tarsal bones supporting the first, second third…
cuttlebone: The shell or bone of cuttlefishes, used for various purposes, as for making polishing powder, etc.
cupper: One who performs the operation of cupping.
cullet: A small central plane in the back of a cut gem. See Collet, 3 (b).
cupel: A shallow porus cup, used in refining precious metals, commonly made of bone ashes (phosphate of lime). [Written also coppel.] Cupel dust, powder used in purifying metals. | To refine by means of a cupel.
cursive: Running; flowing. Cursive hand,a running handwriting. | 1. A character used in cursive writing. 2. A manuscript, especially of the New Testament, written in small, connected characters or in a running hand; -- opposed to uncial. Shipley.
cuckoldom: The state of a cuckold; cuckolds, collectively. Addison.
curvity: The state of being curved; a bending in a regular form; crookedness. Holder.
cundurango: The bark of a South American vine (Gonolobus Condurango) of the Milkweed family. It has been supposed, but erroneously, to be a cure for cancer. [Written also condurango.]
cucurbitaceous: Of, pertaining to, or resembling, a family of plants of which the cucumber, melon, and gourd are common examples.
cutler: One who makes or deals in cutlery, or knives and other cutting instruments.
curacy: The office or employment of a curate.
cubicle: A loding room; esp., a sleeping place partitioned off from a large dormitory.
cunette: A drain trench, in a ditch or moat; -- called also cuvette.
custard: A mixture of milk and eggs, sweetened, and baked or boiled. Custard apple (Bot.), a low tree or shrub of tropical America, including several species of Anona (A. squamosa, reticulata, etc.), having a roundish or ovate fruit the size of a small orange, containing a soft, yellowish, edible pulp. -- Custard coffin, pastry, or crust, which covers or coffins a custard (old) Shak.
cubooctahedron: A combination of a cube and octahedron, esp. one in which the octahedral faces meet at the middle of the cubic edges.
cumbrian: Pertaining to Cumberland, England, or to a system of rocks found there. Cumbrian system (Geol.), the slate or graywacke system of rocks, now included in the Cambrian or Silurian system; -- so called because most prominent at Cumberland.
cubism: A movement or phase in post-impressionism (which see, below). - - Cu"bist (#), n.
cummin: Same as Cumin. Ye pay tithe of mint, and cummin. Matt. xxiii. 23.
cut: 1. To sparate the parts of with, or as with, a sharp instrument; to make an incision in; to gash; to sever; to divide. You must cut this flesh from off his breast. Shak. | 1. To do the work of an edged tool; to serve in dividing or gashing; as, a knife cuts well. 2. To admit of incision or severance; to yield to a cutting instrument.
curable: Capable of being cured; admitting remedy. "Curable diseases." Harvey. -- Cur"a*ble*ness, n. -- Cur`a*bly, adv.
cullis: A strong broth of meat, strained and made clear for invalids; also, a savory jelly. (old) When I am exellent at caudles And cullises . . . you shall be welcome to me. Beau. & Fl. | A gutter in a roof; a channel or groove.
curtaildog: A dog with a docked tail; formerly, the dog of a person not qualified to course, which, by the forest laws, must have its tail cut short, partly as a mark, and partly from a notion that the tail is necessary to a dog in running; hence, a dog not fit for sporting. Hope is a curtail dog in some affairs. Shak.
cull: To separate, select, or pick out; to choose and gather or collect; as, to cuil flowers. From his herd he culls, For slaughter, from the fairest of his bulls. Dryden. | A cully; a dupe; a gull. See Gully.
cuirassier: A soldier armed with a cuirass. Milton.
cubited: Having the measure of a cubit.
cubic: 1. Having the form or properties of a cube; contained, or capable of being contained, in a cube. 2. (Crystallog.) Isometric or monometric; as, cubic cleavage. See Crystallization. | A curve of the third degree. Circular cubic. See under Circular.
cunningly: In a cunning manner; with cunning.
customer: 1. One who collect customs; a toll gatherer. (old) The customers of the small or petty custom and of the subsidy do demand of them custom for kersey cloths. Hakluyt. 2. One who regularly or repeatedly makes purchases of a trader; a purchaser; a buyer. He has got at last the character of a good customer;
cumber: To rest upon as a troublesome or useless weight or load; to be burdensome or oppressive to; to hinder or embarrass in attaining an object, to obstruct or occupy uselessly; to embarrass; to trouble. | Trouble; embarrassment; distress. (old) [Written also comber.] A place of much distraction and cumber. Sir H. Wotton. Sage counsel in cumber. Sir W. Scott.
cunctipotent: All-powerful; omnipotent. [R] "God cunctipotent." Neale (Trans. Rhythm of St. Bernard).
cupidity: 1. A passionate desire; love. (old) 2. Eager or inordinate desire, especially for wealth; greed of gain; avarice; covetousness. With the feelings of political distrust were mingled those of cupidity and envy, as the Spaniard saw the fairest provinces of the south still in the hands of the accursed race of Ishmael. Prescott.
culex: A genus of dipterous insects, including the gnat and mosquito.
cuticular: Pertaining to the cuticle, or external coat of the skin; epidermal.
cuminil: A substance, analogous to benzil, obtained from oil of caraway.
cutwater: 1. The fore part of a ship's prow, which cuts the water. 2. A starling or other structure attached to the pier of a birdge, with an angle or edge directed up stream, in order better to resist the action of water, ice, etc.; the sharpened upper end of the pier itself. 3. (Zoöl.) A sea bird of the Atlantic (Rhynchops nigra);
curia: 1. (Rom. Antiq.) (a) One of the thirty parts into which the Roman people were divided by Romulus. (b) The place of assembly of one of these divisions. (c) The place where the meetings of the senate were held; the senate house. 2. (Middle Ages) The court of a sovereign or of a feudal lord; also; his residence or his household. Burrill. 3. (Law) Any court of justice. 4.
cutty: Short; as, a cutty knife; a cutty sark. [Scot.] | 1. A short spoon. 2. A short tobacco pipe. Ramsay. 3. A light or unchaste woman. Sir W. Scott.
cuckoo: A bird belonging to Cuculus, Coccyzus, and several allied genera, of many species. Note: The European cuckoo (Cuculus canorus) builds no nest of its own, but lays its eggs in the nests of other birds, to be hatched by them. The American yellow-billed cuckoo (Coccyzus Americanus) and the black-billed cuckoo (C. erythrophthalmus) build their own nests.
cuckooflower: A species of Cardamine (C. pratensis), or lady's smock. Its leaves are used in salads. Also, the ragged robin (Lychnis Flos- cuculi).
cucquean: A woman whose husband is unfaithful to her. (old)
cupboard: 1. A board or shelf for cups and dishes. (old) Bacon. 2. A small closet in a room, with shelves to receive cups, dishes, food, etc.; hence, any small closet. Cupboard love, interested love, or that… | To collect, as into a cupboard; to hoard. Shak.
cucullated: 1. Hooded; cowled; covered, as with a hood. Sir T. Browne. 2. (Bot.) Having the edges toward the base rolled inward, as the leaf of the commonest American blue violet. 3. (Zoöl.) (a) Having the prothorax elevated so as to form a sort of hood, receiving the head, as in certain insects. (b) Having a hoodlike crest on the head, as certain birds, mammals, and reptiles.
cubital: 1. Of or pertaining to the cubit or ulna; as, the cubital nerve; the cubital artery; the cubital muscle. 2. Of the length of a cubit. Sir. T. Browne. | A sleeve covering the arm from the elbow to the hand. Crabb.
curious: 1. Difficult to please or satisfy; solicitous to be correct; careful; scrupulous; nice; exact. (old) Little curious in her clothes. Fuller. How shall we, If he be curious, work upon his faith Bean & 2. Exhibiting care or nicety; artfully constructed; elaborate; wrought with elegance or skill. To devise curious works. Ex. xxxv. 32 His body couched in a curious bed. Shak. 3.
curculionidous: Pertaining to the Curculionideæ, or weevil tribe.
cusk: A large, edible, marine fish (Brosmius brosme), allied to the cod, common on the northern coasts of Europe and America; -- called also tusk and torsk.
cuspid: One of the canine teeth; -- so called from having but one point or cusp on the crown. See Tooth.
cuirass: 1. (a) A piece of defensive armor, covering the body from the neck to the girdle. (b) The breastplate taken by itself. Note: The cuirass covered the body before and behind. It consisted of two parts, a breast- and backpiece of iron fastened together by means of straps and buckles or other like contrivances.
custodianship: Office or duty of a custodian.
cumulation: The act of heaping together; a heap. See Accumulation.
curtalfriar: A friar who acted as porter at the gate of a monastery. Sir W. Scott.
cururo: A Chilian burrowing rodent of the genus Spalacopus.
culpon: A shered; a fragment; a strip of wood. (old) Chaucer.
curtal: Curt; brief; laconic. Essays and curtal aphorisms. Milton. Curtal dog. See Curtail dog. | A horse with a docked tail; hence, anything cut short. [Obs] Nares.
cupric: Of, pertaining to, or derived from, copper; containing copper; -- said of those compounds of copper in which this element is present in its lowest proportion.
cultrate: Sharp-edged and pointed; shaped like a pruning knife, as the beak of certain birds.
cultirostres: A tribe of wading birds including the stork, heron, crane, etc.
cucullus: 1. (Bot.) A hood-shaped organ, resembling a cowl or monk's hood, as certain concave and arched sepals or petals. 2. (Zoöl.) A color marking or structure on the head somewhat resembling a hood.
curb: 1. To bend or curve (old) Crooked and curbed lines. Holland. 2. To guide and manage, or restrain, as with a curb; to bend to one's will; to subject; to subdue; to restrain; to confine; | To bend; to crouch; to cringe. (old) Virtue itself of vice must pardon beg, Yea, curb and woo for leave to do him good. Shak.
cuticle: 1. (Anat.) The scarfskin or epidermis. See Skin. 2. (Bot.) The outermost skin or pellicle of a plant, found especially in leaves and young stems. 3. A thin skin formed on the surface of a liquid.
cursitor: 1. A courier or runner. (old) "Cursitors to and fro." Holland. 2. (Eng.Law) An officer in the Court of Chancery, whose business is to make out original writs.
curd: 1. The coagulated or thickened part of milk, as distingushed from the whey, or watery part. It is eaten as food, especially when made into cheese. Curds and cream, the flower of country fare. Dryden. | To cause to coagulate or thicken; to cause to congeal; to curdle. Does it curd thy blood To say I am thy mother Shak.
curare: A black resinoid extract prepared by the South American Indians from the bark of several species of Strychnos (S. toxifera, etc.). It sometimes has little effect when taken internally, but is quickly fatal when introduced into the blood, and used by the Indians as an arrow poison. [Written also urari, woorali, woorari, etc.]
cuneate: Wedge-shaped; (Bot.), wedge-shaped, with the point at the base; as, a cuneate leaf.
curt: Characterized by exessive brevity; short; rudely concise; as, curt limits; a curt answer. The curt, yet comprehensive reply. W. Irving.
curr: To coo. [Scot.] The owlets hoot, the owlets curr. Wordsworth.
cuerpo: The body. In cuerpo, without full dress, so that the shape of the Body is exposed; hence, naked or uncovered. Exposed in cuerpo to their rage. Hudibras.
cutwork: An ancient term for embroidery, esp. applied to the earliest form of lace, or to that early embroidery on linen and the like, from which the manufacture of lace was developed.
cushite: A descendant of Cush, the son of Ham and grandson of Noah.
curmudgeonly: Like a curmudgeon; niggardly; churlish; as, a curmudgeonly fellow.
cubation: The act of lying down; a reclining. (old)
cutworm: A caterpillar which at night eats off young plants of cabbage, corn, etc., usually at the ground. Some kinds ascend fruit trees and eat off the flower buds. During the day, they conceal themselves in the earth. The common cutworms are the larvæ of various species of Agrotis and related genera of noctuid moths.
curio: Any curiosity or article of virtu. The busy world, which does not hunt poets as collectors hunt for curios. F. Harrison.
cuboid: Cube-shaped, or nearly so; as, the cuboid bone of the foot. -- n. (Anat.) The bone of the tarsus, which, in man and most mammals, supports the metatarsals of the fourth and fifth toes.
cucurbit: A vessel of flask for distillation, used with, or forming part of, an alembic; a matrass; -- originally in the shape of a gourd, with a wide mouth. See Alembic.
curvilineal: Consisting of, or bounded by, curved lines; as, a curvilinear figure.
curstness: Peevishness; malignity; frowardness; crabbedness; surliness. (old) Shak.
curcuma: A genus of plants of the order Scitamineæ, including the turmeric plant (Curcuma longa). Curcuma paper. (Chem.) See Turmeric paper, under Turmeric.
cutter: 1. One who cuts; as, a stone cutter; a die cutter; esp., one who cuts out garments. 2. That which cuts; a machine or part of a machine, or a tool or instrument used for cutting, as that part of a mower which severs the stalk, or as a paper cutter. 3. A fore tooth; an incisor. Ray. 4. (Naut.) (a) A boat used by ships of war.
cult: 1. Attentive care; homage; worship. Every one is convinced of the reality of a better self, and of. thecult or homage which is due to it. Shaftesbury. 2. A system of religious belief and worship. That which was the religion of Moses is the ceremonial or cult of the religion of Christ. Coleridge.
curvilinear: Consisting of, or bounded by, curved lines; as, a curvilinear figure.
cutthroat: One who cuts throats; a murderer; an assassin.
cupgall: A kind of oak-leaf gall. See Gall.
cup: 1. A small vessel, used commonly to drink from; as, a tin cup, a silver cup, a wine cup; especially, in modern times, the pottery or porcelain vessel, commonly with a handle, used with a saucer in… | 1. To supply with cups of wine. Cup us, till the world go round. Shak. 2. (Surg.) To apply a cupping apparatus to; to subject to the operation of cupping. See Cupping. 3.
cubit: 1. (Anat.) The forearm; the ulna, a bone of the arm extending from elbow to wrist. (old) 2. A measure of length, being the distance from the elbow to the extremity of the middle finger. Note: The cubit varies in length in different countries, the Roman cubit being 17,47 inches, the Greek 18,20, the Hebrew somewhat longer, and the English 18 inches.
cupreous: Consisting of copper or resembling copper; coppery.
curviserial: Distributed in a curved line, as leaves along a stem.
cuff: 1. To strike; esp., to smite with the palm or flat of the hand; to slap. I swear I'll cuff you, if you strike again. Shak. They with their quills did all the hurt they could, And cuffed the tender… | To fight; to scuffle; to box. While the peers cuff to make the rabble sport. Dryden.
curl: 1. To twist or form into ringlets; to crisp, as the hair. But curl their locks with bodkins and with braid. Cascoigne. 2. To twist or make onto coils, as a serpent's body. | 1. To contract or bend into curis or ringlets, as hair; to grow in curls or spirals, as a vine; to be crinkled or contorted; to have a curly appearance; as, leaves lie curled on the ground.
cupid: The god of love, son of Venus; usually represented as a naked, winged boy with bow and arrow. Pretty dimpled boys, like smiling cupids. Shak.
cully: A person easily deceived, tricked, or imposed on; a mean dupe; a gull. I have learned that . . . I am not the first cully whom she has passed upon for a countess. Addison. | To trick, cheat, or impose on; to deceive. "Tricks to cully fools." Pomfret.
curlycue: Some thing curled or spiral,, as a flourish made with a pen on paper, or with skates on the ice; a trick; a frolicsome caper. [Sometimes written carlicue.] [ Colloq. U.S.] To cut a curlycue, to make a flourish; to cut a caper. I gave a flourishing about the room and cut a curlycue with my right foot. McClintock.
currier: One who curries and dresses leather, after it is tanned.
culls: 1. Refuse timber, from which the best part has been culled out. 2. Any refuse stuff, as rolls not properly baked.
curmudgeon: An avaricious, grasping fellow; a miser; a niggard; a churl. A gray-headed curmudgeon of a negro. W. Irving.
cumucirrostratus: Nimbus, or rain cloud. See Nimbus, and Cloud.
curvative: Having the margins only a little curved; -- said of leaves. Henslow.
cutose: A variety of cellulose, occuring as a fine transparent membrane covering the aerial organs of plants, and forming an essential ingredient of cork; by oxidation it passes to suberic acid.
cupshake: A shake or fissure between the annual rings of a tree, found oftenest near the roots.
curarine: A deadly alkaloid extracted from the curare poison and from the Strychnos toxifera. It is obtained in crystalline colorless salts.
culture: 1. The act or practice of cultivating, or of preparing the earth for seed and raising crops by tillage; as, the culture of the soil. 2. The act of, or any labor or means employed for, training,… | To cultivate; to educate. They came . . . into places well inhabited and cultured. Usher.
cumulatist: One who accumulates; one who collects.
curriculum: 1. A race course; a place for running. 2. A course; particularly, a specified fixed course of study, as in a university.
culicid: Like or pertaining to the Mosquito family (Culicidæ). -- n. A culicid insect.
cud: 1. That portion of food which is brought up into the mouth by ruminating animals from their first stomach, to be cheved a second time. Whatsoever parteth the hoof, and is cloven-footed, and cheweth the cud, among the beasts, that shall ye eat. Levit. xi. 3 2. A portion of tobacco held in the mouth and chewed; a quid. [Low] 3. The first stomach of ruminating beasts. Crabb.
cutoff: 1. That which cuts off or shortens, as a nearer passage or road. 2. (Mach.) (a) The valve gearing or mechanism by which steam is cut off from entering the cylinder of a steam engine after a definite point in a stroke, so as to allow the remainder of the stroke to be made by the expansive force of the steam already let in. See Expansion gear, under Expansion.
cusp: 1. (Arch.) A triangular protection from the intrados of an arch, or from an inner curve of tracery. 2. (Astrol.) The beginning or first entrance of any house in the calculations of nativities, etc. | To furnish with a cusp or cusps.
culminate: 1. To reach its highest point of altitude; to come to the meridian; to be vertical or directly overhead. As when his beams at noon Culminate from the equator. Milton. 2. | Growing upward, as distinguished from a laterral growth; -- applied to the growth of corals. Dana.
cudgel: A staff used in cudgel play, shorter than the quarterstaff, and wielded with one hand; hence, any heavy stick used as a weapon. He getteth him a grievous crabtree cudgel and . . . | To beat with a cudgel. An he here, I would cudgel him like a dog. Shak. To cudgel one's brains, to exercise one's wits.
curiologic: Pertaining to a rude kind of hieroglyphics, in which a thing is represented by its picture instead of by a symbol.
cucumis: A genus of plants including the cucumber, melon, and same kinds of gourds.
culpe: Blameworthiness. (old) Banished out of the realme . . . without culpe. E. Hall.
curacoa: A liqueur, or cordial, flavored with orange peel, cinnamon, and mace; -- first made at the island of Curaçcao.
curtain: 1. A hanging screen intended to darken or conceal, and admitting of being drawn back or up, and reclosed at pleasure; esp., drapery of cloth or lace hanging round a bed or at a window; | To inclose as with curtains; to furnish with curtains. So when the sun in bed Curtained with cloudy red. Milton.
cuckold: 1. A man whose wife is unfaithful; the husband of an adulteress. Shak. 2. (Zoöl.) (a) A West Indian plectognath fish (Ostracion triqueter). (b) The cowfish. | To make a cuckold of, as a husband, by seducing his wife, or by her becoming an adulteress. Shak.
cursor: Any part of a mathematical instrument that moves or slides backward and forward upon another part.
cuprite: The red oxide of copper; red copper; an important ore of copper, occurring massive and in isometric crystals.
cur: 1. A mongrel or inferior dog. They . . . like to village curs, Bark when their fellows do. Shak. 2. A worthless, snarling fellow; -- used in contempt. What would you have, you curs, That like nor peace nor war Shak.
cutinization: The conversion of cell walls into a material which repels water, as in cork.
customableness: Quality of being customable; conformity to custom. (old)
cunabula: 1. The earliest abode; original dwelling place; originals; as, the cunabula of the human race. 2. (Bibliography) The extant copies of the first or earliest printed books, or of such as were printed in the 15th century.
curried: 1. Dressed by currying; cleaned; prepared. 2. Prepared with curry; as, curried rice, fowl, etc.
cubiform: Of the form of a cube.
cupola: 1. (Arch.) A roof having a rounded form, hemispherical or nearly so; also, a celing having the same form. When on a large scale it is usually called dome. 2. A small structure standing on the top of a dome; a lantern. 3. A furnace for melting iron or other metals in large quantity, -- used chiefly in foundries and steel works. 4.
cue: 1. The tail; the end of a thing; especially, a tail-like twist of hair worn at the back of the head; a queue. 2. The last words of a play actor's speech, serving as an intimation for the next… | To form into a cue; to braid; to twist.
cullion: A mean wretch; a base fellow; a poltroon; a scullion. "Away, base cullions." Shak.
cumulate: To gather or throw into a heap; to heap together; to accumulate. Shoals of shells, bedded and cumulated heap upon heap. Woodward.
curialistic: 1. Pertaining to a court. 2. Relating or belonging to the ultramonate party in the Latin Church.
cubile: The lowest course of stones in a building.
curtesy: the life estate which a husband has in the lands of his deceased wife, which by the common law takes effect where he has had issue by her, born alive, and capable of inheriting the lands. Mozley & W.
cupful: As much as a cup will hold.
cubeb: The small, spicy berry of a species of pepper (Piper Cubeba; in med., Cubeba officinalis), native in Java and Borneo, but now cultivated in various tropical countries. The dried unripe fruit is much used in medicine as a stimulant and purgative.
cutlass: A short, heavy, curving sword, used in the navy. See Curtal ax. Cutlass fish, (Zoöl.), a peculiar, long, thin, marine fish (Trichirus lepturus) of the southern United States and West Indies; -- called also saber fish, silver eel, and, improperly, swordfish.
custodian: One who has care or custody, as of some public building; a keeper or superintendent.
cube: 1. (Geom.) A regular solid body, with six equal square sides. 2. (Math.) The product obtained by taking a number or quantity three times as a factor; as, 4x4=16, and 16x4=64, the cube of 4. | To raise to the third power; to obtain the cube of.
cussedness: Disposition to willful wrongdoing; malignity; perversity; cantankerousness; obstinacy. [Slang or Colloq., U. S.] In her opinion it was all pure "cussedness." Mrs. Humphry Ward. Disputatiousness and perversity (what the Americans call "cussedness"). James Bryce.
